subject: Skyline Retail — policy matrix & fallback choreography (post-call)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@skylineretail.io>, Mike Torres <mike@skylineretail.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Skyline Retail — policy matrix & fallback choreography (post-call)

Hi Laura / Mike,

Thanks again for taking the call today — this summary captures the key architecture asks and our recommended next steps so your engineering and procurement teams have something concrete to work from. I split this into (A) quick decisions we need from you, (B) recommended config for Redwood, and (C) next steps + timeline.

A) Decisions we need from Skyline (please highlight in-line):
- Primary region for low-latency reads: you said "US-East (N. Virginia)" — confirm?
- Cost target: do you want to prioritize p95 latency <=150ms even if cost increases ~10%? Or prefer a strict cost cap?
- Data policy: can we send product descriptions + SKU (no PII) to hosted inference? Any legal constraints?

B) Recommended configuration (high level):
1) SDK & auth
   - Use our Node + Python SDKs (we'll provide a pinned sample) and service account API key for server-side calls.
   - For client-side browse features, use short-lived tokens via your backend.
   - We will add a scoped key for reranker/embedding read-only so your frontend cannot initiate expensive writes.

2) Model routing & policy matrix (proposed)
   - Route by intent: search -> embedding+rerank; chat/helpdesk -> opt-gen model; bulk enrichment -> quantized batch model.
   - Latency policy: p95 <=150ms (US-East) for search rerank. If p95 >150ms, fall back sequence: a) smaller-generation variant (8-bit quantized), b) alternative region (US-West) if latency improves, c) synchronous cached result (serve previous top-3 for 100ms budget).
   - Cost policy: if per-request token cost for reranker > $0.005, apply 2-tier sampling (shorter context + aggregated rerank) to reduce cost.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - We'll enable structured JSON outputs for your product-extraction step. Use Redwood's tool-calling schema to return: {"sku_lookup": {"sku": string, "confidence": number}}. (We'll share the exact schema file.)

4) Embeddings & reranker strategy
   - Use 1536-d embeddings (dense) stored in your vector DB; Redwood will return a reranker score and normalized logits to merge with your business signals.
   - Cache embeddings for 24h; rerankers should call Redwood rerank endpoint with top-100 retrievals.

C) Next steps + timeline
- Today: confirm region + data policy.
- Wed (Jan 20): Redwood will send SDK quickstart patch and policy-matrix-draft.xlsx.
- End of week: joint tech-check (30m) to validate end-to-end demo.

Attachments: integration-probing-sample.csv (sample queries), policy-matrix-draft.xlsx (config draft).

Thanks — looping Ben and Laura (internal) to pick the tech-check slot.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0118

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Laura Chen <laura@skylineretail.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline Retail — policy matrix & fallback choreography (post-call)

Thanks Tessa — +1 on the summary. A few technical clarifications from my side (Rishi, feel free to add):

- SDK / auth
  * Quickstart: we'll provide a small patch (attached: sdk-quickstart.patch) that wires up Node and Python examples and a cURL. Example server call (Node):

    const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_SVC_KEY });
    const res = await client.rerank({ model: 'rrk-small-v1', candidates: candidatesArray });

  * For scoped keys: we'll create two keys for your account: rerank-readonly and embeddings-write (for backfill).

- Routing policy specifics
  * The "fallback chain" should be configurable per-route. We'll add a policy YAML you can version: route: search -> policy: ["rrk-prod-v2","rrk-quant-v1","regional-fallback"].
  * Regional fallback: the routing table will prefer region-level pools; if US-East latency SLO violated and US-West >10% faster, auto-route. We'll expose real-time SLOs in the console and an event webhook for failover.

- Structured output
  * We'll provide a schema file and a preflight validator. When the model returns malformed JSON we can auto-apply a deterministic extractor (syntactic fallback) to avoid blocking your pipeline.

- Embeddings & reranker ops
  * Reranker returns normalized scores (0-1) and a token-length estimate to help you compute cost. We'll include a sample merge function.

I'll follow up with the policy YAML and a minimal terraform snippet if you want Redwood Dedicated later. 

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@skylineretail.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Torres <mike@skylineretail.io>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline Retail — policy matrix & fallback choreography (post-call)

Tessa / Ben — thanks for the clear write-up. Short answers:

- Region: confirm US-East (primary). We will allow fallbacks to US-West but please keep any EU routing disabled (our legal team flagged EU egress).
- Latency vs cost: prioritize latency for search rerank (p95 <=150ms). For background enrichment jobs we want cost-optimized runs.
- Data policy: no customer PII to be sent to hosted endpoints. Product metadata and public-facing descriptions are OK. We will send a sanitized sample dataset by EOD Tuesday.
- Procurement: procurement wants an initial SOW + price estimate before Feb 2. Can you provide a ballpark monthly committed cost for the search rerank route at 20M queries/month?

We can join a tech-check Wed 20th at 11am PT — Mike will be the engineering lead on our side.

Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Product | Skyline Retail

Subject: Re: Skyline Retail — policy matrix & fallback choreography (post-call)

Great — thanks for the confirmations, Laura. Quick action items and owners before the Wed tech-check 11am PT:

- Tessa: send the policy-matrix-draft.xlsx and a short SOW + ballpark pricing (attached).
- Ben & Rishi: create policy YAML + sdk-quickstart.patch; prepare a 15-min demo that shows: 1) rerank happy path with <150ms, 2) demo of fallback to quantized model, 3) structured output validator.
- Mike: send sanitized sample dataset (CSV) to secure-drive link and confirm no PII.
- Procurement question (Laura): we will provide a committed cost estimate for 20M queries/month by EOD Tue (attached estimate in the draft SOW).

Attachments: policy-matrix-draft.xlsx, sdk-quickstart.patch, SOW-ballpark.pdf (attachment stubs).

If anything changes for Wednesday, flag here and we'll reschedule. Looking forward to the tech-check.

Best,
